business_problem: Siemens lacked a unified way to see and secure thousands of distributed OT assets across factory floors, which made vulnerability prioritization, firmware updates, and lifecycle planning too slow for a highly variable production environment.
solution_summary: At Siemens' Bad Neustadt electric-motor factory, ServiceNow became the bridge between OT and IT operations. The solution combines Siemens Industrial Asset Hub and SINEC Security Guard with ServiceNow OT Visibility and OT Vulnerability capabilities so factory teams can discover assets, assess firmware risk, and manage remediation from one operational view. OT data is fed into the Configuration Management Database, where lifecycle status, dependencies, and replacement information become visible alongside IT context. Service teams can then remotely connect to devices, apply approved updates, document each action, and verify authorization without losing production traceability. The result is an operational-security layer that does more than inventory machines: it connects vulnerability analysis, patching, lifecycle management, and future agentic-AI use cases on a single platform designed to protect uptime in complex manufacturing environments.

solution_components.name: Industrial Asset Hub
solution_components.role: Supplies detailed OT asset and lifecycle data from the factory floor.

solution_components.name: SINEC Security Guard
solution_components.role: Provides the OT security signals used to identify firmware and vulnerability risk.

solution_components.name: OT Visibility
solution_components.role: Gives Siemens a unified operational view for monitoring and managing OT assets alongside IT context.

solution_components.name: Configuration Management Database
solution_components.role: Stores OT asset relationships, lifecycle information, and dependency context used for remediation planning.

data_flow: Industrial Asset Hub and SINEC Security Guard feed OT asset and risk data into ServiceNow, where OT Visibility and the CMDB combine that information with IT context. Teams then identify vulnerable devices, plan updates, remotely apply authorized firmware or configuration changes, and use the same system to track lifecycle and replacement needs.
business_outcome: Siemens expects to identify and prioritize vulnerabilities 90% faster, reduce security-fix time by 38%, accelerate OT asset onboarding into the CMDB by 70%, and improve lifecycle planning and production uptime by bringing OT and IT data into one management plane.
